items.content_text:
A great example of teamwork — and giving something a second life! ⚽️🌱
 Hamilton County Parks & Recreation was proud to partner with Chattanooga Football Club and the City of Chattanooga to help relocate sod originally used at Erlanger Park for a professional soccer match to its new home at East Lake Park.
 Our Parks crew helped haul and transport the grass to East Lake, where it could be reused to refresh the soccer area and improve playing conditions for the community.
 Instead of seeing a valuable resource go to waste, partners came together, rolled up their sleeves and found a way to put it right back to work for local families and athletes.
 We love seeing collaboration like this turn into a visible community improvement. The before ➡️ during ➡️ after transformation speaks for itself!
 Thank you to Chattanooga Football Club, the City of Chattanooga and everyone who helped make it happen.
 #HamiltonCountyParks #EastLakePark #ChattanoogaFC #CommunityPartnership #Teamwork #ChattanoogaTN #ParksAndRecreation
From the professional pitch to the community field! 
 The East Lake Park soccer area is looking great after a much-needed refresh!
 The sod originally used at Erlanger Park for a CFC professional soccer match was donated and given a second life at East Lake Park, helping us repair and improve the playing area for the community.
 This is a great example of what can happen when partners work together. CFC, the City of Chattanooga, and Hamilton County Parks & Recreation came together to turn used sod into a valuable community improvement.
 From before ➡️ during ➡️ after, the transformation speaks for itself!
 Thank you to everyone who helped make this partnership possible and helped bring better playing conditions to East Lake Park.

 Parks should be places where everyone belongs, and today is another important step toward that goal. 💚

items.content_text:
Getting to class can be one of the most routine parts of a student’s day, but the hassle of parking, navigating Chattanooga’s heat and long walks across campus can throw that routine off. For students looking to ease these burdens, UTC offers the Mocs Express shuttle as a convenient, safe way to get around campus free of charge. 🚌 
 The Mocs Express shuttle operates a regular 13-hour route Monday through Friday, with a special Friday evening route for students to enjoy. Starting at Engel Stadium, the Mocs Express runs through campus and the neighboring streets for a complete loop of less than 30 minutes. Once the bus returns to its starting point, the route restarts.
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/your-ride-around-campus-getting-to-…/

items.content_text:
YEARS IN THE MAKING: Congratulations to CFD Captain Skyler Phillips and many caring community partners on the grand opening of the Harvesting Inclusive Playground at Jack Benson Heritage Park!
 Captain Phillips spearheaded the project, which is now the largest fully accessible playground in the Chattanooga area. A custom farm-themed playground was designed with universal accessibility at its core, ensuring children of all physical abilities can play together without barriers.
 Designed for ages 2–12, the park features fully ramped play structures, wheelchair-accessible carousel elements, adaptive swings, sensory enrichment stations, and seamless rubber surfacing for barrier-free play.
 It’s a model project for excellence for other designs like it at other parks and playgrounds!

An undercover operation was conducted alongside the execution of a search warrant for the business. Authorities arrested a female employee, identified as Wei Guang Han, during the operation, and evidence identified as being used for the furtherance of crime to include money, was seized during the investigation.
 Han was transported to the Hamilton County Jail & Detention Center and faces the following charge: 
 • Prostitution
 Direct any questions to the TBI and Homeland Security Investigations. View the TBI's news release here: https://tbinewsroom.com/…/statewide-operation-addresses-il…/.

Today, Hamilton County EMS joins our nation in solemn remembrance of the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.
 Twenty-five years have passed, but we have not forgotten the 2,977 lives lost, including the firefighters, law enforcement officers, EMS professionals, and other first responders who answered the call that morning—many making the ultimate sacrifice while trying to save others.
 We remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable tragedy. We remember the families whose lives were forever changed. And we honor those who continued to serve in the days, months, and years that followed, many suffering lasting effects from their service at Ground Zero.
 For those of us in emergency services, September 11 remains a powerful reminder of what it means to answer the call—to run toward those who need us when others are running away.
 On this 25th anniversary, the men and women of Hamilton County EMS pause to remember, honor, and reflect.
 May we never forget September 11, 2001. 
 343 Firefighters.
 37 Port Authority Police Officers.
 23 NYPD Officers.
 8 EMS Professionals.
 And thousands of innocent lives.
 We will never forget.

Devonta Shepherd (DOB: 11/03/94) was taken into custody and transported to the Hamilton County Jail and Detention Center. He is charged with Attempted 1st Degree Murder, Aggravated Assault, Unlawful Possession (Felon), and Employing a Firearm During the Commission of a Dangerous Felony.
The information is preliminary and is subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.
The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct and not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.
###
Original Release:
CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. – The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a shooting that occurred at approximately 09:45 a.m. in the 400 block of Tunnel Blvd.
Officers responded to a report of a person being shot. Upon arrival, officers located a 41-year-old male with a gunshot wound. Officers rendered medical aid before EMS transported the victim to a local hospital for a potentially non-life-threatening injury.
CPD Homicide and Crime Scene Units responded to investigate and process the scene. No suspect information is currently available.
This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.

A collaboration of researchers from UTC and Marmara University in Türkiye has received a U.S. design patent for a wearable device designed for people with essential tremor—a neurological movement disorder that can make routine tasks such as writing, eating, drinking, dressing and using a computer more difficult.
 The patent covers the ornamental design for an upper-extremity tremor control device developed through a partnership that began nearly three years ago. The device fits around a user’s wrist and forearm and uses a modular design intended to accommodate different body sizes and needs.

Sheriff Austin Garrett and the men and women of the HCSO stand with the Knox County Sheriff’s Office as they mourn the passing of retired Sheriff Tom Spangler. 
 “Retired Sheriff Tom “Spanky” Spangler was a friend, a leader, a mentor, and the definition of strength and courage to me and many other law enforcement professionals across our great state. He served Knox County with true servant leadership, and his passing is a tremendous loss not only to Knox County but to every sheriff in this state; my prayers and condolences go to the Spangler family and his KCSO family. We’re proud to celebrate Cassie Davis, Hamilton County Schools’ Manager for Climate and Capacity Building, on her selection for Leadership Chattanooga’s 2026 cohort!

Selected as one of 45 community leaders, Cassie is spending the next 10 months learning alongside professionals from across Chattanooga as part of a leadership development experience focused this year on Growth-Minded Leadership.

The journey kicked off with a two-day retreat in Knoxville, where the cohort explored leadership styles, trust, collaboration and what it means to help create high-performing, high-learning cultures. But for Cassie, one of the most meaningful parts of the experience has been the relationships she’s already building with people from across the community.

 Two historic brick homes in the Park Place neighborhood are headed to auction, offering new owners the chance to breathe new life into a pair of Victorian-era houses in the heart of Chattanooga.
 Park Place is an important part of the historic fabric surrounding the MLK Boulevard corridor, and properties like these help give the neighborhood its distinctive character and sense of place.

 Historic houses don’t have to be frozen in time. With the right investment, they can be adapted for contemporary life while retaining the character that makes them irreplaceable.

The challenges shaping Tennessee’s future are regional, and so are many of the solutions.

Members of our SETD team traveled to Nashville yesterday for the 2026 ThinkTennessee Policy Forum, joining leaders from across the state for conversations around workforce development, transportation, housing, energy and economic growth.

From navigating growth across Tennessee’s counties to strengthening the workforce pipeline and preparing for increasing energy demand, the day offered valuable perspectives on many of the same opportunities and challenges we see here in Southeast Tennessee.

The #OECD headline inflation was broadly stable at 4.1% in July 2026, as energy inflation stabilised above 10%. Increases in headline inflation across 13 OECD countries were largely balanced by declines in 14, while rates remained broadly stable in 11.
 Year-on-year energy inflation within the OECD and core inflation (inflation excluding food and energy) were broadly stable at 11.6% and 3.6%, respectively, although energy inflation remained above 10% for the fourth consecutive month.
 Food inflation declined in 23 OECD countries in July, including falls of 2.0 percentage points (p.p.) or more in Greece, Hungary and Latvia. As a result, OECD food inflation fell to 3.2% in July, after 3.4% in June.

items.title: Commission Meeting Summary — September 8, 2026  Vacation & Comp Time Policies — The commission approved Resolution 579,...
items.content_text:
Commission Meeting Summary — September 8, 2026 
 Vacation & Comp Time Policies — The commission approved Resolution 579, updating the vacation accrual schedule for key management/department heads, aimed at helping the city stay competitive in attracting and retaining experienced leaders. Resolution 580 was also approved, removing the previous 5-year cap on compensatory time accrual for non-exempt hourly employees. 
 Flag Policy Adopted — After weeks of discussion sparked by local American Legion and VFW representatives, the commission approved Resolution 581, adopting a formal city-wide flag policy. The policy sets flag sizing based on flagpole height (the "one-quarter rule") and calls for a 20'x38' U.S. flag at Veterans Memorial Park's 125-ft pole — down from the current oversized flag, which veterans groups said posed a safety risk to handlers, was causing wear on the equipment, didn't conform to flag code, and hung too low at half-staff. Commissioner Howse requested preserving flexibility to fly a larger flag for special occasions; after the vote, City Manager Holmes noted that flexibility is already built in, since a future commission can authorize a larger flag via resolution. Several citizens also spoke against the change, noting the memorial flag has flown for around 22 years. 
 Courtroom Dedication — Commission approved Resolution 582, renaming the City Hall courtroom the "Judge Kevin B. Wilson Memorial Courtroom," honoring his 35 years on the bench (1990–2025). Judge Wilson passed away in January 2026. 
 Structural Cabling Bid — Commission approved awarding the City Hall cabling upgrade project to Ontivity, LLC, the lowest of five bids received (~$59,869), to replace outdated network/phone cabling. 
 Airport Advisory Board — From 12 applicants, the commission approved the top four vote-getters (Jack Farrow, John Record, Heath Merz, and Michael Brown), then broke a three-way tie for the fifth seat in favor of Zoe Krohne. Final appointments will be formalized by resolution at the September 21 meeting. 
 License Plate Reader (Flock) Contract — Following growing national concerns regarding use of LPR technology — and after a local law enforcement agency suspended its own use of the technology — the commission voted to withdraw from its contract with Flock Safety, following a formal recommendation from Collegedale Chief of Police and city administration. Police access to the cameras had already been revoked pending this discussion. 
 Withdrawal involves per-camera removal fees (~$500 each) offset by prorated fee refunds, with cameras to come down within a "reasonable timeframe" after written notice. Flock cameras are also used by private organizations and on private property. These are not regulated by the City of Collegedale or any other government entity, and the city has no right to remove them since they are not installed or controlled within city right-of-way. Public comment was largely opposed to the cameras, citing constitutional concerns and privacy worries. 
 Other Notes — Commission discussed finalizing a date for the Christmas Parade (leaning toward a survey to gauge community preference among Nov. 21, Nov. 28, or Dec. 5, and whether to pair it with the Christmas tree lighting). Staff is also pursuing CPR certification for employees and coordinating with the Health Department on a mobile vaccination van for tetanus shots. Brief updates were given on the playground project, railroad camera project, and right-of-way work on Little Debbie Parkway. 
 View the meeting recording here: https://www.collegedaletn.gov/…/agenda…/livestream/index.php

The Unifi Aviation team that operates Delta Air Lines flights at CHA just received the Mike Schwartz Operational Excellence Award for the second quarter of 2026!!🥳
 Presented to only a few Delta stations annually by Delta's Operations & Customer Center (OCC) leadership, this highly competitive award recognizes teams that go above and beyond in operational and customer experience. Over the past few months, the team stepped up to safely welcome an unusually high number of flights rerouted to CHA because of weather at other airports. 
 We're so proud to partner with this team and Delta at CHA🩵 Help us congratulate them on this VERY well-deserved recognition!!
